content.value_statement: Teams need reliable API inventories across services, versions, and environments. This skill gives .NET SDK workflows for Azure API Center governance and discovery.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install Azure.ResourceManager.ApiCenter and Azure.Identity packages.
Creates API Center services, workspaces, APIs, versions, definitions, environments, and deployments.
Imports and exports API specifications through the .NET management SDK.
Defines metadata schemas for API governance fields and assignments.
Lists APIs, versions, environments, and deployments from a workspace.
Provides basic Azure RequestFailedException handling patterns.
limitations: Does not provision Azure credentials, subscriptions, or resource groups.
Does not validate OpenAPI, GraphQL, or other specification contents.
Uses example names and URLs that must be replaced for production.
Focuses on .NET SDK usage, not Azure CLI or portal workflows.

use_cases.title: Create an API Inventory
use_cases.description: Set up services, workspaces, and API records for a team API catalog.

use_cases.title: Govern API Metadata
use_cases.description: Define required metadata such as team, cost center, and data classification.

use_cases.title: Document Deployments
use_cases.description: Link API definitions to runtime environments and deployment records.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the packages, environment variables, and authentication setup needed for Azure API Center with the .NET SDK.

prompt_templates.title: Create Inventory Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an Azure API Center service, workspace, API, version, and definition for a REST API.

prompt_templates.title: Add Governance Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an API Center metadata schema for team ownership, cost center, and data classification using Azure.ResourceManager.ApiCenter.

prompt_templates.title: Model Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a .NET workflow that links an API definition to a production environment and lists the deployed APIs afterward.

output_examples.input: Create an API Center service and workspace for engineering APIs.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step .NET SDK workflow that authenticates with DefaultAzureCredential, creates the service, and adds an engineering workspace.

output_examples.input: Add governance metadata for API ownership.
output_examples.output: A metadata schema plan covering owning team, cost center, and data classification, with guidance for required assignments.

output_examples.input: List APIs and deployments in a workspace.
output_examples.output: A concise traversal approach that reports API titles, versions, environments, deployment names, and deployment states.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder name, URI, and resource identifier before using examples in production.
Use managed identity and DefaultAzureCredential where possible for Azure authentication.
Keep lifecycle stage, version, metadata, and deployment records aligned with the real API state.
anti_patterns: Do not store subscription IDs, resource group names, or service names as shared secrets.
Do not upload API specifications that have not been reviewed for sensitive data.
Do not expose raw Azure exception details directly to application users.

faq.question: What Azure service does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure API Center management through the Azure.ResourceManager.ApiCenter .NET package.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and workflows that a developer can adapt and run in their own Azure environment.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it show?
faq.answer: It shows DefaultAzureCredential from Azure.Identity for standard Azure SDK authentication flows.

faq.question: Can it manage API specifications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for importing and exporting API specifications through API definition resources.

faq.question: Is it limited to REST APIs?
faq.answer: No. The reference table includes REST, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP, webhook, WebSocket, and MCP API kinds.

faq.question: Does it replace Azure API Management?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on API inventory and governance, while Azure API Management handles gateway and policy functions.
